event_scope: 2026-10-29 Binance hot-wallet signing compromise; XRP Ledger theft tranche and subsequent cross-chain laundering; issuer freeze response for RLUSD, USDC and USDT.

receipt_policy.stored_hash_scope: Hashes cover the exact evidence paraphrase strings stored in this artifact. Transaction hashes are identifiers reported by the cited trace; XRPLScan returned HTTP 403 in this retrieval, so the underlying transaction JSON was not independently downloaded.

evidence_paraphrases.text: Binance says five of its hot wallets transferred 233.46 million XRP to one attacker-controlled XRPL account between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC on 29 October.
Binance says the attacker used a compromised engineer endpoint and an internal AI tool to reach other engineers' machines and obtain a deployment permission token.
Binance's 3 November update says 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of 31 October and more than 100% of required loss coverage was reserved.

limitations: The incident report is Binance's own account; Binance says some technical details remain confidential and independent firms would review the findings.
The 98% replenishment statement is aggregate across impacted token assets; it does not establish that Binance bought 233.46M XRP in the spot market.
The report describes compromised endpoints, credentials/deployment permission and wallet-signing access; it does not establish that an LLM itself was compromised or autonomously signed transactions.

evidence_paraphrases.text: The FBI officially attributes the Binance theft of more than $6 billion to the DPRK cyber activity it calls TraderTraitor.
The public FBI alert lists Ethereum, Bitcoin and Solana addresses but does not list the XRPL attacker account identified by the on-chain tracing sources.

limitations: The public alert does not publish the FBI's underlying attribution evidence or a transaction-level XRPL account mapping.
The FBI attribution is an official assessment, not a judicial finding; public blockchain data alone cannot identify the human controller.

evidence_paraphrases.text: North Korea denied responsibility for the Binance theft and characterized the FBI attribution as a provocation.
AP also reported President Trump saying investigators had not yet established whether North Korea was responsible.

limitations: The denial is a reported state position; it does not independently disprove the FBI attribution.

evidence_paraphrases.text: Panoptic says every amount, address and time is its own read of public blockchains; for XRPL it reads each Payment's delivered amount and result.
A 42.75 million RLUSD payment to the new XRPL account failed at 20:04:52 UTC because the destination account did not yet exist.
Panoptic traces 233.46 million XRP from five Binance wallets to one new XRPL account; its account split on 2 November reached seven new accounts.
One recipient later sent 26.96 million XRP to 19 accounts; three deposited 6.55 million XRP into THORChain, which paid 75.89 BTC.
At least 1.42 million XRP in those THORChain deposits came from other senders, so the full 75.89 BTC output cannot be attributed to the Binance theft.
At 02:37 UTC on 6 November, Panoptic's eight tracked accounts held 206.50 million XRP; it had read only five of the 19 downstream accounts in full.

limitations: The source's latest XRP read is 03:25 UTC on 6 November, not current at the 7 November capture.
XRPLScan proof links returned HTTP 403 in this retrieval; transaction JSON was not independently downloaded.
Panoptic says only five of 19 downstream accounts were read in full; some recipients mix stolen XRP with unrelated senders.
Panoptic's $2.65B frozen total is an address-level read at its cutoff, not Binance's broader frozen-or-intercepted accounting.

evidence_paraphrases.text: Elliptic estimates about 42 million XRP had left by 08:45 UTC on 6 November and about 192 million XRP remained.
Elliptic's 08:00 UTC 7 November update says about 44 million more XRP left overnight and about 148 million XRP remained.
Elliptic says the laundering is automated but has seen no evidence of an AI agent making decisions.
Elliptic says blockchain traces identify wallets and movements, not the human controller behind them.

limitations: Elliptic's address attribution and cross-chain clustering are proprietary; the public article does not provide every underlying transaction receipt.
Its 148M XRP remaining figure is an approximate tracked balance at 08:00 UTC on 7 November.
Elliptic says a negligible amount has likely been cashed out; most activity is conversion between public-chain assets, not fiat realization.

evidence_paraphrases.text: Bitquery reports 44.2 million XRP swapped out by 10:00 UTC on 6 November, equal to 19% of the stolen XRP tranche.
Bitquery says THORChain carried about 113 million dollars, split between 57 million dollars from XRP and 56 million dollars from TRON.
By its cutoff, Bitquery traced 620 BTC paid to 28 Bitcoin addresses by XRP swaps; other routes also paid those addresses.
Bitquery counts each coin once at first exit and counts only the attacker's share when wallets contain mixed funds.

limitations: The full XRP transaction history is sold as a dataset; this run used the public investigation summary only.
Bitquery says 71 million dollars went to wallets it did not follow and three ownership calls move the total laundering estimate between 315 million and 344 million dollars.
Its first-exit method differs from Elliptic's and Panoptic's account-level tracing; do not add the BTC output to XRP amounts or double-count later hops.

evidence_paraphrases.text: The 30 October article said the 233.46 million XRP had not moved from the initial attacker account as of its publication snapshot.

limitations: Its no-movement statement was true only for its 30 October cutoff; it is superseded by observed 2 November splitting and 5–7 November cross-chain activity.

event_timeline.event: A Binance wallet attempted a 42.75M RLUSD payment to the new XRPL destination; it failed because the account did not exist.
The first 185.02M XRP payment created the destination XRPL account.
Five Binance hot wallets transferred a total 233.4619431 XRP million to one new XRPL account.
Circle froze 823M USDC at the main Ethereum receiving address before the source says any of it had been swapped.
Ripple paused 40.54M RLUSD on Ethereum after approximately 48M RLUSD had been swapped away.
The original attacker account redistributed all but 23.7 XRP to new XRPL accounts; Panoptic reports seven recipients while Elliptic reports six.
One recipient sent 26.96M XRP in 122 payments to 19 accounts; a tracked subset deposited 6.55M XRP into THORChain.
Elliptic estimated about 42M XRP had left and about 192M remained.
Bitquery estimated 44.2M XRP had left the original chain, 19% of the stolen tranche.
Elliptic estimated 44M additional XRP had left overnight and about 148M remained.

interpretation.cross_chain_route: Most of the later XRP movement was swapped through THORChain into BTC; this is a cross-chain conversion, not proof of centralized-exchange sale or fiat cashout.
interpretation.current_cashout_status: Elliptic says only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out as of its 7 November 08:00 UTC update.
interpretation.panoptic_output_attribution: The 75.89 BTC Panoptic traced from its 6.55M XRP deposit subset is contaminated by at least 1.42M XRP from other senders; do not attribute all 75.89 BTC to the theft.
interpretation.scale: The approximately 86M XRP movement is about 36.8% of the original stolen tranche, but it is not equivalent to 86M XRP sold on centralized order books.

ripple_rlusd.caveat: This is RLUSD on Ethereum, distinct from the failed 42.75M RLUSD payment to a not-yet-created XRPL account.

circle_usdc.caveat: Circle's $1.1B statement does not list addresses; Panoptic's 824.7M is its read of attacker addresses and is not the full Circle incident scope.

tether_usdt.caveat: The 669M is combined USDT converted to ETH/TRX before freezes; it is not XRP.

incident_scope_disagreement.note: These totals use different chain coverage, wallet scopes and valuation cutoffs. The XRP tranche itself is consistently reported at 233.46M XRP; do not average incident totals.

attribution.us_president_public_comment: Said investigators had not yet established responsibility
attribution.on_chain_identity_limit: Blockchain traces establish transfers and wallet relationships, not the human identity or nationality of the controller.

binance_reported_attack_chain: Compromised engineer endpoint through tampered developer tooling.
Separate engineer targeted through a fake recruitment/interview assignment and malware.
Internal AI tool used as a pivot to reach additional engineer machines.
Attacker obtained a container/software deployment permission token.
Access reached Binance's internal wallet signing service.
what_is_not_established: No evidence in the reviewed sources that an LLM model itself was exploited through prompt injection.
No evidence that an AI agent independently decided to transfer funds or held a signing key.
Elliptic describes the laundering as conventional automation and says it has seen no evidence of AI-agent decision-making.

existing_on_1640_not_main: Issue-triggered autonomous writer workflows quarantined with empty permissions.
Coinbase paper-trader changed to explicit YES, exact-main-SHA, read-only artifact output.
designed_not_verified: Separate agent runtime credentials from deployment and wallet-signing credentials.
No persistent deployment token in agent-visible environment or workspace.
Short-lived identity tokens and task-scoped least privilege.
Read-only default for research and analysis agents.
Human dual control for any external write or privileged operation.
Immutable audit receipts for tool calls and permission changes.

cross_source_reconciliation.xrp_amount: Binance, Panoptic, Elliptic and Bitquery all anchor the initial XRP tranche at approximately 233.46M XRP.
cross_source_reconciliation.account_count: Panoptic reports seven new recipients on 2 November; Elliptic reports six. Unresolved, likely a tracking/definition difference; retain both.
cross_source_reconciliation.laundering_progress: Panoptic's 6.55M XRP THORChain trace is a subset from three downstream accounts and an earlier cutoff. Bitquery's 44.2M XRP first-exit estimate at 10:00 UTC 6 November and Elliptic's 42M at 08:45 UTC are close but use different labels/methods. Elliptic's later 44M additional outflow through 08:00 UTC 7 November is a later observation, not a direct contradiction.
cross_source_reconciliation.freeze_amount: Panoptic reads $2.65B frozen on attacker addresses; Binance and Elliptic report $2.85B frozen/intercepted. Scope, timing and intercepted-versus-frozen definitions differ.
cross_source_reconciliation.cashout: Elliptic reports negligible fiat cashout by 08:00 UTC 7 November; Bitquery counts first exit from chain as laundered, not necessarily fiat cashout.
cross_source_reconciliation.source_independence: Binance and FBI are primary institutional statements; AP reports political positions; Panoptic, Elliptic and Bitquery are separate on-chain analytics pipelines over overlapping public ledgers. Their estimates are independent analyses, not independent underlying transactions.

reasons: The stolen XRP is a security-event outflow from Binance hot wallets, not ordinary customer withdrawals or a normal exchange-flow observation.
Subsequent movement is cross-chain swapping through THORChain, not proof of centralized order-book sales.
Analytics providers use different address sets, cutoffs and ownership labels; some destination accounts mix funds from unrelated senders.
No direct evidence establishes fiat cashout or the effect on consolidated XRP spot depth.
The event must be timestamped and evaluated as a one-off security shock before any predictive feature use.

next_actions: Fetch and hash direct XRPL public-node transaction JSON for the five Binance outflows, failed RLUSD attempt, recipient splits and THORChain deposit proofs; XRPLScan was HTTP 403 in this run.
Track the 148M XRP Elliptic balance at the next public update and reconcile with Bitquery's first-exit definition; do not add BTC outputs to XRP amounts.
Measure THORChain XRP pool depth, swap size, price impact and fees at the actual deposit times before estimating market impact.
Check Binance Proof of Reserves XRP liabilities and hot-wallet/cold-wallet balances separately; do not infer 233M XRP repurchase from aggregate 98% replenishment.
Keep issuer freeze events for RLUSD/USDC/USDT separate from native XRP transfers and freeze capabilities.
